description:
Fold BP-7 — the finding the 2026-09-03 re-run of `kcb-subscription-firehose.md` returned, and one of the two blockers on KCB count (iv).

VERIFIED AGAINST THE TEXT (2026-09-12, before this tasklist was authored).

THE REFUSAL IS STATED AT REGISTRATION ONLY. §4.2b's normative bullet reads: 'A producer that cannot honour a declared limit MUST refuse the subscription AT REGISTRATION, with a stated reason, rather than accept it and exceed it. Fail closed, as everywhere else on this bus (§5, §7.2).' That is the whole of the producer's obligation, and it is scoped to one moment.

BUT THE OPERANDS ARE EXPLICITLY LIVE-ADJUSTABLE. §4.2b's own preamble says the operands are 'set at registration AND ADJUSTABLE IN-BAND (d)', and §4.2d's subscriber→producer direction spells out what that means: 'set or adjust the (b) operands on a live subscription: slow down, pause, resume, change `on_overflow`. This is what makes the subscription adjustable without a teardown, and it is the lever Step 3 of the leg went looking for and did not find.' So the contract mints a lever, and says nothing about what the producer OWES when it is pulled.

WHICH IS ONE PARAGRAPH SHORT OF §4.2c'S OWN DISCIPLINE. §4.2c fixes exactly this shape for `resume`: 'A producer MUST answer a `resume` in exactly one of three ways, and SILENCE IS NOT ONE OF THEM: (i) resume from that point; (ii) refuse `gap-unavailable`, naming the earliest point it can resume from; or (iii) refuse `resume-unsupported`. A producer that cannot resume is conformant; a producer that silently starts at now while a `resume` was asked for is NOT.' A live adjustment has no such rule, so a saturated subscriber that pulls the lever cannot tell *honoured* from *ignored* — and a lever whose effect is unobservable is the disconnect §4.2b was written to replace.

THE FOLD. Additive, KCB-only, §4.2b and §4.2d: say what a producer owes a live adjustment on the control channel, in §4.2c's own shape — honour it, or refuse it with a stated reason, and silence is not one of them. Nothing here becomes a quality-of-service contract (§4.2g stands: KCB fixes the SHAPE of what may be asked and what must be answered; scheduling, queue discipline, buffer sizing and admission policy stay in each participant's own infra), the host stays off the path (ADR-0001), and a subscription that declares none of §4.2's operands is a 0.4.6 subscription served as one.

THEN RE-RUN COUNT (iv). BP-8 also gates count (iv) and lands in `950`, which is why this depends on it: one walk over text carrying both findings, rather than two walks each re-reading the other's absence.

userStories.title: A producer owes a live adjustment an answer, and silence is not one of them
userStories.description: Extend §4.2b's fail-closed discipline past registration, in the shape §4.2c already uses for `resume`.
acceptanceCriteria: §4.2b (with §4.2d) states what a producer owes an adjustment made on the live control channel: honour it, or refuse it with a stated reason — and SILENCE IS NOT ONE OF THEM, in the same terms §4.2c fixes for `resume`. A producer that cannot honour a live adjustment stays conformant by refusing; one that silently ignores it is not.

The clause is written so the SUBSCRIBER can tell the outcomes apart, which is the property the lever needs to be a lever: §4.2d's whole rationale is that a stalled transport window is unattributable and therefore unassertable, and a frame is preferred precisely because KCS §5's vocabulary can range over it.
The existing registration-time rule is preserved unchanged, and the new clause is stated as the same rule extended rather than a second convention: fail closed, as §5 and §7.2 do.

§4.2g is untouched and re-affirmed: this fixes the SHAPE of the answer, not a latency, a rate, or a liability. Scheduling, queue discipline, buffer sizing, admission policy and the retry curve stay in each participant's own infra.

userStories.title: Additive, peer-to-peer, and no new mechanism
userStories.description: The fold must ride what §4.2d already mints. A second signalling path would contradict the clause it is folding into.
acceptanceCriteria: The answer rides §4.2d's EXISTING in-band control channel in the producer→subscriber direction. No new verb, no new transport, no second connection, and §4.1's audit is unchanged — `subscribe` remains the one session-shaped clause.

The ignore-what-you-do-not-understand rule still holds: a subscriber MUST tolerate a producer that never sends one, and an unknown frame is ignored — which is what keeps §4.2 additive and a 0.4.6 participant interoperable.

It composes across §3.1 federation for §4.2d's stated reason — the binding, and therefore its channel, runs directly between the two peers, and no party with jurisdiction over both ends was ever required (ADR-0001).

Lossy versus lossless is not disturbed: a producer MAY apply a lossless adaptation unasked and MUST NOT apply a lossy one that was not asked for, and a retraction is never shed. Verified against §4.2b's text rather than assumed.

The KCB version move is decided under §7.2's own table and recorded with reasoning; if it moves, all three status mirrors (`README.md`, `specs/README.md`, `ECOSYSTEM.md`) move with it, and §2.3's legacy namespace-root removal declared at KCB 0.6.0 is checked rather than tripped.
